result.summary: The intersection features high-visibility zebra crosswalks, dedicated pedestrian signals, and well-maintained brick sidewalks. While the environment is generally pedestrian-friendly, the wide one-way street lacks physical traffic calming measures to manage vehicle speeds.

hazards.name: Wide travel lanes
hazards.description: The width of the one-way street may encourage higher vehicle speeds through the intersection.

hazards.name: Turning vehicle conflict
hazards.description: Vehicles turning onto the one-way street may conflict with pedestrians in the crosswalk.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and slow turning vehicles.

interventions.title: Raised Crosswalk
interventions.description: Elevate the crosswalk to the level of the sidewalk to prioritize pedestrians and act as a speed table.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the signal to give pedestrians a head start before vehicles get a green light.

result.summary: The image shows a residential street with sidewalks on both sides but no visible marked crosswalks or pedestrian safety infrastructure. Parked vehicles on the right side and a brick wall on the left create potential sightline issues for pedestrians attempting to cross.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: There are no designated or marked areas for pedestrians to cross the street safely.

hazards.name: Visual obstructions from parked cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the right curb block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians who might step into the street.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks with high-visibility patterns to designate pedestrian crossing points.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at intersections to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces near intersections or crossing points to improve sightlines for all road users.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by well-marked high-visibility crosswalks and functional pedestrian signals at a signalized intersection. While sidewalks are in good condition and curb ramps are present, the wide curb radius and utility poles at the corner create potential sightline and speed-related hazards.

hazards.name: Corner Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: A large utility pole at the corner may partially block the view of pedestrians for approaching drivers.

hazards.name: Wide Turning Radius
hazards.description: The curb radius allows for relatively high-speed vehicle turns, increasing risk to pedestrians in the crosswalk.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at the corner to reduce crossing distance and slow turning traffic.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking near the intersection to improve visibility for all road users.

result.summary: The intersection is equipped with high-visibility zebra crosswalks, curb ramps, and pedestrian signals. The presence of sidewalks on both sides and mature street trees creates a defined pedestrian realm, though the crossing distance remains moderate without physical bulb-outs.

hazards.name: Unprotected crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of potential traffic without a median refuge or curb extensions to shorten the exposure time.
